scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF
from each other!! From the department head's machine (it_hod) none of the CS
computers (the 192.168.2.x ones) answer any more -- our own department is
fine, it's just CS that's gone. The router that joins the two departments has
obviously dropped one of its sides -- it's still talking to us but it has let
go of CS, one hundred percent!! Please plug the CS side back into the router
and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claims that the IT department (it_hod, 192.168.1.x) has lost all connectivity to the CS department (192.168.2.x) and that router0 has "dropped" its CS-facing interface. A complete multi-layer investigation found no evidence of any such fault.

**Affected component:** None. All subsystems are operating normally.

**Mechanism (why no fault exists):** Router0 is the sole inter-departmental router. Its eth0 (192.168.1.1/24) connects the IT LAN via switch0, and its eth1 (192.168.2.1/24) connects the CS LAN via switch1. Both interfaces are in UP/UP state with correct IP assignments. The routing table carries both subnets as directly-connected kernel routes. The routing protocol (RIP) supplies all inter-site routes (to router1/router2 subnets) correctly.

**Localization:** No device is implicated. `l2_snapshot` confirmed all 30 device interfaces are UP with no duplicate MACs. `infra_sweep` found zero ACL/firewall rules, no static ARP spoofing, and no addressing anomalies. `tc_snapshot` found zero traffic-shaping qdiscs. `pressure_sweep` found no resource stress on any device.

**Verification:** Live pings from it_hod to cs_hod (192.168.2.2) and cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3) both completed at **0% packet loss**. The path it_hod → router0 → CS subnet is fully operational.

**Root cause:** There is no fault. The connectivity between the IT and CS departments is intact and functioning correctly at the time of this investigation.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The helpdesk ticket appears to be based on an incorrect observation or a transient issue that has since resolved on its own.
